notes: Parallel subagent cap runs to 128, and one spawn_agent call starts up to 16 agents. rules.ts raises maxParallel's bound from 32 to 128 on both the rules schema and a thread tune; the Orchestration settings picker (OrchestrationRules.tsx) and the thread tune stepper (ThreadTune.tsx) offer 32, 64 and 128. spawn_agent (orchestration.ts) takes either `task` for one agent or `agents` (SPAWN_BATCH_MAX = 16 entries, each with its own task; the top-level provider/model/reasoning/agentType/context1m/useWorktree are defaults an entry may override). Every entry is resolved before any is created, so a bad model or an empty task in slot seven refuses the whole call naming `agents[6]`; the parallel and total caps count the whole batch and the refusal says how many fit; worktrees are added one after another with the slot in the tag so a batch never races git for index.lock or shares a path; a batch answers `{ agents: [{agentId, title, cwd, findingsFile?}], parallel, note }` while a single spawn keeps its shape. The same schema reaches codex through scripts/app-mcp-bridge.mjs (SPAWN_SPEC shared by the call and each entry) and the WS contract (SpawnAgentSpecSchema in contract.ts); the orchestrator prompt says a fan-out is one call. The renderer's spawn row (appTool.ts) reads "Spawned N agents" for a batch. Tests: orchestration (batch in order with per-entry overrides, one-entry batch keeps the single shape, 17 refused, bad slot refuses all and names it, empty task, parallel cap across a batch with the free count, 128 admits a full batch over 100 live, total cap across a batch), appTool batch row, shared/rules bounds (128 in, 129 out).
